title: Time-Frequency Representations (TFR) Dashboard
note: Covers STFT, Wavelet (CWT/DWT), spectrogram, and scalogram methods used in EEG seizure analysis. High-priority feature gap addressed 2026-08-06.

methods.name: Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT)
methods.notes: Fixed window = time-frequency uncertainty trade-off. Best for stationary EEG segments.

methods.name: Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT)
methods.notes: Adaptive resolution — superior for non-stationary EEG transients (spikes, HFOs).

methods.name: Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)
methods.notes: Fast O(n) — used in real-time edge deployment. PyWavelets backend.

methods.name: Power Spectrogram (STFT magnitude²)
methods.notes: Log-scaled power improves CNN convergence. Used in EEGNet / 1D-CNN pipelines.

methods.name: Mel Spectrogram
methods.notes: Mel warping weights low frequencies more — useful when delta/theta dominate seizure signal.

methods.name: Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD/SPWVD)
methods.notes: Highest TF resolution but cross-term interference. SPWVD kernel removes artifacts.

frequency_bands.seizure_relevance: ripples + fast ripples — epileptogenic zone marker

definitions.definition: Short-Time Fourier Transform — segments signal into overlapping windows, computes FFT per window. Produces time-frequency spectrogram with fixed resolution.
Continuous Wavelet Transform — convolves signal with scaled/translated wavelets (Morlet). Adaptive resolution: better time resolution at high frequencies.
Discrete Wavelet Transform — dyadic subband decomposition using filter banks. Fast O(n), used for denoising and feature extraction.
2D plot of |STFT|² — power (dB) vs time (x) vs frequency (y). Standard CNN input format for seizure classification.
Spectrogram with frequency axis warped to mel scale — perceptually motivated, emphasises low-frequency content relevant to epileptic delta/theta bands.
2D plot of |CWT|² — power vs time vs scale (analogous to frequency). Reveals transient high-frequency events like HFOs.
High-Frequency Oscillation (80–500 Hz) — ripples (80–250 Hz) and fast ripples (250–500 Hz) are biomarkers of epileptogenic zones detectable via CWT/WVD.
Gaussian-modulated complex sinusoid — default CWT mother wavelet for EEG analysis. Optimal time-frequency localisation per Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
Smoothed Pseudo Wigner-Ville Distribution — quadratic TFR with kernel smoothing to suppress cross-term interference. Highest resolution among TFR methods.
Integral of power spectral density over a frequency band. Derived from STFT or DWT coefficients. Primary feature for classical ML seizure classifiers.
